'''Romeo Langford''' (born October 25, 1999) is an American [[basketball]] player. He played college basketball for [[Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball|Indiana Hoosiers]]. Langford was ranked as one of the highest prospects in the high school class of 2018 and drew interest from many notable colleges before committing to play for the Indiana Hoosiers in [[2018–19 Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball team|2018–2019 season]].<ref name=LangfordDecision>{{cite web|title=Romeo Langford decision: Mr. Basketball picks IU|url=https://www.indystar.com/story/sports/high-school/2018/04/30/langford-announcement/559263002/|website=Indianapolis Star|accessdate=30 April 2018|language=en}}</ref>

==High school career==
Langford attended New Albany High School. Despite substantial interest from multiple prep schools, Langford chose to spend his four high school years at New Albany.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.courier-journal.com/story/sports/preps/indiana/2017/11/27/romeo-langford-never-considered-leaving-new-albany/898417001/ |title=Romeo Langford says he never considered leaving New Albany for a prep school |work=[[The Courier-Journal]] |date= November 27, 2017 |access-date= November 27, 2017 |last=Winstead |first=Kenzie}}</ref> As a freshman, Langford led New Albany to a 23–3 record and the regional tournament while averaging 17.1 [[Point (basketball)|points]] and 6.0 [[Rebound (basketball)|rebounds]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.indystar.com/story/sports/high-school/2016/03/16/total-package-langford-drawing-comparisons-bailey/81863476/ |title=‘Total package’ Romeo Langford drawing comparisons to Damon Bailey |work=[[The Indianapolis Star|Indy Star]] |date= March 16, 2016 |access-date= November 28, 2017 |last=Neddenriep |first=Kyle}}</ref> In his sophomore year, he averaged 30.2 points, 9.0 rebounds, and 3.0 [[Assist (basketball)|assists]] per game while leading New Albany to a 27–1 record and a class 4A state championship, the school's first state title since 1973. In his junior year, he averaged 28.7 points, 8.9 rebounds, and 3.4 assists per game, leading New Albany to a 25–4 record and to the class 4A state quarterfinals. On November 21, 2017, Langford opened up his senior season with a then career high 48 points in a 110–36 victory over Charlestown.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.slamonline.com/college-hs/high-school/top-5-recruit-romeo-langford-drops-48-points/#H0LK42JubA42HelT.97 |title=Top 5 Recruit Romeo Langford Drops 48 Points |work=[[Slam (magazine)|SlamOnline.com]] |date= November 22, 2017 |access-date= November 25, 2017}}</ref> On February 1, Langford scored a new career high 63 points against Jennings County. abilities.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.news-sentinel.com/sports/2017/12/11/romeo-langford-series-managing-the-circus/ |title=NS on Romeo Langford, Part I: Managing the circus |date= December 11, In addition, he was also named the Boys Athlete of the Year.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.indystar.com/story/sports/high-school/2018/04/29/romeo-langford-wins-indiana-mr-basketball-indiana-sports-awards/559072002/|title=Romeo Langford of New Albany earns IndyStar Indiana Mr. Basketball|date=April 29, 2018 |access-date=April 29, 2018 |first=Kyle |last=Neddenriep |work=[[The Indianapolis Star|Indy Star]]}}</ref>

Langford was recruited in high school by numerous high-profile schools, including [[University of Indiana|Indiana]], [[University of Louisville|Louisville]],
[[University of Kansas|Kansas]], [[University of Kentucky|Kentucky]], [[Vanderbilt University|Vanderbilt]], [[University of North Carolina|North Carolina]], [[University of California, Los Angeles|UCLA]], and [[Duke University|Duke]],<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.indystar.com/story/sports/high-school/2017/04/07/battle-romeo-langford/100173088/ |title=The Battle for Romeo Langford is on |work=[[The Indianapolis Star|IndyStar]] |date= April 9, 2017 |access-date= November 26, 2017 |last=Neddenriep |first=Kyle}}</ref> and was visited by multiple coaches including [[John Calipari]], [[Bill Self]], [[Roy Williams (coach)|Roy Williams]], and [[Archie Miller (basketball)|Archie Miller]].<ref name=Langfordinterview /><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.courier-journal.com/story/sports/college/indiana/2017/12/08/indiana-archie-miller-romeo-langford-new-albany-floyd-central/936803001/ |title=Indiana coach Archie Miller checks out Romeo Langford in New Albany-Floyd Central game |work=[[The Courier-Journal]]
|date= December 8, 2017 |access-date= December 9, 2017 |first=Gentry |last=Estes}}</ref> On November 11, 2017, Langford announced via [[Twitter]] that he had narrowed his choices down to Indiana, Kansas, and Vanderbilt.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.crimsonquarry.com/2017/11/11/16637718/romeo-langford-trims-his-list-to-indiana-vanderbilt-and-kansas |title=Romeo Langford trims his list to Indiana, Vanderbilt, and Kansas |date= November 11, 2017 |access-date= November 21, 2017 |last=Grossman |first=Jack}}</ref> When asked about a timeline for his decision, Langford emphasized that he didn't want to rush the decision, and that he would "probably be making [his] decision after the season."<ref>{{cite web |url=https://scout.com/college/basketball/recruiting/Article/QA-with-five-star-guard-Romeo-Langford-108660549 |title=Q and A with Five Star Guard Romeo Langford |date= October 9, 2017 |access-date= November 21, 2017 |work=[[Scout.com]] |last=Daniels |first=Evan}}</ref> He announced on April 11, 2018 that he would declare his college choice on April 30 at New Albany High School.<ref>{{cite web |url=Romeo Langford announces date for college pick between Kansas, Vanderbilt and Indiana |title=Romeo Langford announces date for college pick between Kansas, Vanderbilt and Indiana |date= April 11, 2018 |access-date= April 19, 2018 |work=courier journal |last=Page |first=Fletcher}}</ref> On April 30, 2018, he announced his intention to play for his home state Indiana University.<ref name=LangfordDecision />

==College career==
Langford has been named Big Ten Freshman of the Week four times.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://bigten.org/news/2019/1/14/indiana-and-maryland-earn-weekly-mens-basketball-honors.aspx?path=mbball |title=Indiana and Maryland Earn Weekly Men’s Basketball Honors |work=Big Ten |date= January 14, 2019 |access-date= February 4, 2019}}</ref> He is averaging 17 points per game, the highest among Big Ten freshmen and the third highest all-time among Indiana University freshmen, behind [[Eric Gordon]] and [[Mike Woodson]].<ref>Ohio State @ IU CBS Broadcast, 10 February 2019</ref>

After the season, Langford declared for the [[2019 NBA draft]], where he is a projected lottery pick.<ref>http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/26439940/indiana-freshman-langford-says-enter-draft</ref>

==Personal life==
Romeo is the son of Tim and Sabrina Langford, and has two sisters, Tiffany and Tisha.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.insidethehall.com/2018/05/03/q-a-romeo-langfords-mother-sabrina-langford/ |title=Q & A: Romeo Langford’s mother, Sabrina Langford |work=insidethehall.com |date= May 3, 2018 |access-date= May 3, 2018 |last=Bozich |first=Alex}}</ref> He began playing basketball in the first grade, and has expressed admiration for NBA player [[LeBron James]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nbadraft.net/romeo-langford-interview |title=Romeo Langford Interview |work=NBADraft.net |date= August 28, 2017 |access-date= November 28, 2017 |last=Makris |first=Stefanos}}</ref> Romeo has expressed pride in challenging himself academically through advanced classes and enjoyment in taking math, and noted that he desires a college that would allow him to get a good degree in addition to playing basketball.<ref name=Langfordinterview>{{cite web |url=https://www.courier-journal.com/story/sports/college/kentucky/2017/05/07/meet-new-albanys-shooting-star-romeo-langford/101165568/ |title=Meet New Albany's Shooting Star Romeo Langford |work=[[The Courier-Journal]] |last=Page |first=Fletcher |date= May 8, 2017 |access-date= November 22, 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.newsandtribune.com/sports/romeo-the-person-langford-remains-grounded-during-rise-to-fame/article_8d3c9b1e-d86b-11e6-8eb9-53c32c501083.html |title=ROMEO THE PERSON: Langford remains grounded during rise to fame |work=[[News and Tribune]] |date= January 13, 2017 |access-date= November 28, 2017 |last=Maskulinski |first=Justin}}</ref>  He is a close friend of college football All-American [[Rondale Moore]] as the two grew up together on the same block in New Albany and played basketball together through their sophomore year of high school.<ref>https://www.indystar.com/story/sports/columnists/gregg-doyel/2018/12/18/ius-romeo-langford-purdues-rondale-moore-were-buddies-new-albany/2335083002/</ref>
